Subject: Brightwell Health — Access integration & orchestration (SSO / SCIM / IP rules / service accounts)

Hi Alexandra / Brightwell team,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for your inference stack. I wanted to start a single thread to track the access-integration work so it's easy to hand off between CS, implementation, and infra. Attached is a first-pass mutual action plan and a SAML metadata example for reference.

Top-level asks to unblock our infra prep: 
- Confirm IdP vendor and metadata (we need saml assertion consumer URL and entity ID).
- SCIM scope: do you plan to sync users only or groups + nested groups? Any group filter we should apply?
- IP allowlist ranges for both test and prod (include static NATs).
- Service account pattern: who will own the service account(s) that call our admin APIs? Do you require short-lived tokens or long-lived keys?
- Org policies / lockboxes: any org-wide require-2FA exemptions we should know about?

I've cc'd Jonas and Karthik from our implementation team and Monica who will run the pre-cutover checklist on the day. Proposed timeline: infrastructure prep + test cutover next week, production cutover the week after (dates flexible based on your availability).

Attachments: Brightwell_Onboarding_MAP_v1.xlsx, saml-sample-metadata.xml

Next step: can you return your IdP metadata and a bullet list for the IP ranges by EOD tomorrow? We'll slot the test cutover once we have those.

Thanks,

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks Soojin — looping in our IT ops contact for technical details. Quick answers below: 

- IdP: Okta (we'll attach the metadata). See bw_idp_metadata.xml.
- SCIM: We'll do user + group sync. We currently sync top-level groups only; nested groups are rare but we can enable if Redwood needs it.
- IP allowlist: Test NATs: 34.210.12.0/24, 34.210.13.0/24. Prod NATs: 52.30.44.0/24, 52.30.45.0/24. We'll confirm if Gov zone affects these.
- Service accounts: We'll create a dedicated service account brightwell-redwood-admin@brightwell.health that will own SCIM provisioning and call the Redwood admin endpoints. We prefer short-lived tokens; if Redwood supports automatic rotation we can adopt that.
- Org policies: No company-wide 2FA exemptions; MFA enforced for all accounts.

Attaching: bw_idp_metadata.xml

Great — thanks for the quick answers, Alex. A few technical notes and asks from the infra side before we schedule the test cutover:

1) SCIM token lifecycle: We recommend issuing a scoped SCIM token with a 30-day lifetime and a rotation webhook. If Brightwell prefers short-lived tokens, we can accept a 12-hour token but will need a rotation endpoint configured.

2) Group sync: If nested groups are off by default, please send a sample membership CSV for the two groups you plan to sync to validate mapping for RBAC on our side.

3) IP allowlist staging: We'll need the test NATs added to our staging allowlist by 2025-09-15 23:59 UTC. Can IT Ops confirm who will open the firewall/ACL ticket and the change window?

4) Service account naming: please confirm the service account will be brightwell-redwood-admin@brightwell.health and that it will be able to mint tokens via your internal STS. If STS isn't available, we can use long-lived keys stored in an encrypted vault.

5) Pre-cutover smoke tests: We'll run an automated smoke that exercises SAML login, SCIM create/update/delete of a test user, and an IP-restricted API call. Expected runtime: ~18 minutes. Monica will coordinate the runbook.
